public_rationale: Contemporaneous evidence shows meaningful gains rather than a general capability plateau. Independent vision-language comparisons and OlympicArena both favor newer frontier models over predecessors. Anthropic also reports a substantial coding gain on its internal evaluation. These findings do not show that hallucinations or reliability problems were solved. The judgment applies to stalled capability improvement, not to the stronger claim that existing methods could become fully reliable.
limitations: Arena preferences can reflect presentation as well as correctness.
The coding evaluation was conducted by the model's developer.
The quarter-based target period is an explicit interpretation of an undated ongoing observation.

our_interpretation: Current approach refers to neural generative AI, especially frontier language models.
The plain reading is that meaningful capability gains across successive frontier releases had stalled.
The claim supplies no reporting period. I use April–June 2024, the latest completed calendar quarter before the post, to assess the ongoing state.
A plateau in capability is different from continued errors or failure to attain perfect reliability.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evaluations across recent frontier releases show no meaningful improvement across substantive capabilities.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous comparable evaluations show meaningful frontier gains across substantive tasks, including independent evidence.

evidence.explanation: User comparisons collected June 10–25 show newer frontier models outperforming preceding models on image-containing conversations. Preference measurements are imperfect, but this is independent evidence of improvement within the target quarter.

OlympicArena independently finds a clear gap favoring the newer models on difficult multidisciplinary problems. The same abstract says overall performance remains unsatisfactory; that limits claims of reliability but does not establish stalled improvement.
